models_evaluated: machine learning-based tool to assist physical therapists

links.outcome: Pain response, mental health, engagement, satisfaction and adverse events with AI-supported care versus DCP alone
links.effect: Pain response 64% vs 63% (p=0.399); anxiety p=0.928; depression p=0.187; adverse events 0.58% vs 0.69% (p=0.231). Outcomes were similar, so AI-supported scaling did not compromise outcomes.
links.quote: Similar improvements in pain response were observed, regardless of the group (response rate: 64% vs. 63%; p = 0.399).

unlisted_practices: Scaling clinician-to-patient ratio (2.3-fold) using an AI tool to assist physical therapists in digital MSK care

screen.reason: Evaluates a real-world digital care deployment comparing patient outcomes and safety with vs without an AI clinical decision support tool allowing scaled provider-to-patient caseloads.

primary.practice: AI-assisted clinical workflow for PT scaling
